prompt: A casting reference portrait of a fictional Indian man of about thirty-four, front-facing, from the waist up, against a plain mid-grey backdrop with soft even light from both sides. Medium-brown skin, short wavy black hair parted on his left, a thick black moustache, light stubble, and a small pale scar cutting through his right eyebrow. He wears a plain white cotton shirt with sleeves rolled to the elbow and a steel kada on his right wrist. Neutral expression, eyes to the lens, 85 mm perspective.

A costume department reference photo: a 1940s Telugu village woman's costume shown on two headless dress forms side by side against a plain light-grey backdrop, front view on frame left, back view on frame right. An indigo handloom cotton sari with a mustard checked border, draped in the local style with the pleats at the front and the end over the left shoulder; a maroon cotton blouse with elbow-length sleeves; a pair of plain silver anklets placed on the floor in front of each form. Soft even studio light, true colours, 50 mm.

The front verandah of an old tiled-roof house in Kerala during monsoon rain, late afternoon. An elderly woman of about seventy-five sits in a long-armed wooden easy chair, angled three-quarters towards frame left, holding a steel tumbler in both hands. She has grey hair in a low bun, round wire-rimmed spectacles, and wears an off-white cotton sari with a thin dark-green border. Her skin is deep brown with fine wrinkles. Two square wooden pillars stand at frame left and frame right; a tall brass oil lamp, unlit, stands to the left of the chair. The floor is polished red oxide. Beyond the verandah, rain falls in sheets off the roof edge and a coconut palm and green garden blur behind it. Soft grey daylight from the garden side, frame left. Camera at seated eye level, 50 mm, the woman in the centre-right third.

An on-model catalogue photo for a fictional ethnic-wear label, Neela. A fictional Indian woman of about twenty-six with a medium-brown complexion, shoulder-length wavy black hair and small silver jhumka earrings stands facing the camera, weight on her left leg, against a warm beige paper backdrop. She wears a mustard cotton straight kurta reaching her knees, with a small white block-printed floral pattern, three-quarter sleeves and a round neck with a short placket of five white buttons; white cotton palazzo pants; a white mulmul dupatta over her left shoulder that hangs crookedly. A small safety pin is visible at the kurta's right hem. Soft daylight from a large window at frame left. Full length, 70 mm, 4:5.

A catalogue flat-lay of a fictional Kanchipuram-style silk saree on a pale grey surface, shot from directly above. The saree is folded to show three parts side by side: on the left, the body in deep peacock green (close to #0F5257) with small gold buttis in a diamond grid; in the middle, the border, a 12 cm magenta (close to #B0186A) band with a gold temple-tower pattern; on the right, the pallu in magenta with broad gold stripes and a row of gold peacocks. A matching magenta blouse piece is folded on top of the body. Even soft light. 50 mm.

A packshot of three glass spice jars from a fictional Madurai brand, Aadi, in a row on a white surface, straight on. Each jar has a black lid and a kraft-paper label. The labels read, left to right: "மஞ்சள்" over "TURMERIC"; "மிளகாய்" over "CHILLI"; "சீரகம்" over "CUMIN"; each with "Aadi" in a small terracotta wordmark at the top and "100 g" at the bottom. The jars show their contents: bright yellow powder, deep red powder, whole brown seeds. Soft light from upper left. 85 mm.

A casting reference portrait of a fictional Indian woman of about twenty-eight, front-facing, from the waist up, against a plain mid-grey backdrop with soft even light. Dusky medium-dark brown skin, long black hair in a single low braid over her left shoulder, a small gold stud in her left nostril, a small mole just above the right corner of her upper lip, and a thin black-bead mangalsutra. She wears a plain mustard cotton kurta. Neutral expression, eyes to the lens, 85 mm perspective.

A painted game portrait of an original elderly sage character, chest up, three-quarter view facing frame right, against a warm ochre background. About eighty, with deep brown wrinkled skin, a long white beard tied with a single wooden bead, a shaved head with three ash lines across the forehead, one cloudy left eye, a rudraksha mala around his neck, and a saffron shawl. Soft light from upper left. Painterly, visible brush strokes.

A character reference for a fictional snack-brand mascot, Chotu Mirchi, front view, full body, standing on a plain white background, in a polished 3D animated style. Chotu is a glossy red chilli about as tall as a child's forearm, standing upright on two short green legs, with a curled green stalk on top like a quiff that curls to his left. Big round white eyes with black pupils, thick black eyebrows, a wide grin showing one gold tooth on his right side. Thin green arms with white four-fingered gloves. White sneakers with red laces. Soft even studio light, a soft shadow under his feet.

A product packshot of a fictional chips pack, Mirchi Mood, on seamless white, front face to camera, standing slightly puffed with natural crinkles at the top and bottom seals. The pack is glossy red with a yellow sunburst in the centre; in the sunburst sits the face of the chilli mascot (big round eyes, grin with one gold tooth); above it the brand name "Mirchi Mood" in chunky white rounded letters with a black outline; below, a green flag reading "Masala Blast"; bottom right a white circle reading "₹20"; bottom left "52 g". Soft top light, a gentle highlight along the top crinkle. 85 mm, pack centred.

A North Indian haldi ceremony in the open courtyard of an old haveli, late morning, soft bright overcast daylight. Exactly six people. The bride, mid-twenties, sits centre-left on a low carved wooden stool in a plain yellow cotton suit, face and forearms smeared with turmeric paste, laughing with eyes half closed. Standing behind her on frame left, her mother in a green sari pours water from a brass lota over her head. Kneeling on frame right, two cousins in pink kurtas rub turmeric on her arms. On the far right edge an elderly grandfather in a white kurta and grey Nehru jacket sits on a cane chair, clapping. Behind the bride, a boy of about eight in an orange kurta holds a large brass bowl of turmeric paste. Strings of marigold hang across the top of the frame; a sandstone arch fills the back wall; the stone floor is splashed yellow. Camera at standing eye level, 35 mm, slightly to the right of centre.

Sand dunes in the Thar desert just after sunrise. A rider sits on a standing dark-bay horse with the inward-curving ear tips of a Marwari horse, seen in full side profile facing frame right. The horse has a white blaze down its face and one white sock on the front left leg; a red and gold woven saddle cloth. The rider, a man of about forty with a thick moustache, wears a white kurta, white dhoti and an orange turban. The sun sits just above the dunes at frame left, so long shadows of horse and rider stretch towards frame right across rippled sand. Camera low at the horse's knee height, 85 mm, horse and rider on the right third.

A painted game illustration of a war-tiger mount, Vyaghra, in side profile facing frame right on a sunlit savanna at golden hour. A huge Bengal tiger with one torn left ear, a white scar across its right eye, and a pattern of stripes that forms a clear "V" shape on its forehead. It wears a turquoise and brass saddle with a red tasselled saddle cloth and a small leather saddle bag on its left flank. Warm sun from frame left, long shadow to the right. Painterly style, visible brush strokes.

Key art for an original squad game, illustrated in a clean cel-shaded style, daylight on a dusty Rajasthani fort rampart. Exactly five characters stand in a line, left to right: a tall bearded man with a shield and a blue turban; a short young woman with goggles and a drone on her shoulder; a heavy-set older man with a grey moustache and a rocket launcher; a lean woman archer with a white braid and a green scarf; and a teenage boy with a skateboard and red headphones. A saffron banner flies from a pole behind the middle character. Sun high and to the left; short shadows to the right.

A film set dressed as a 1970s middle-class Indian drawing room, empty of people, shot from the doorway at standing eye level with a 24 mm perspective. Exact layout: the back wall is pale green; in its centre stands a wooden radio cabinet with a fabric speaker grille, and above it hangs a framed black-and-white wedding photograph. On frame left, a three-seat teal vinyl sofa sits under a window with white lace curtains, afternoon daylight coming through them. On frame right, a rattan armchair, and beside it a brass floor lamp with a cream shade. In the centre of the room, a low wooden coffee table holding a glass ashtray, a folded newspaper and a clear plastic water bottle. On the right wall, a modern white modular switchboard. The floor lamp holds a cool-white LED bulb that is switched on. The floor is red-and-black checkered tiles; a ceiling fan with three brown blades hangs at the top.

An in-game screenshot without any interface of a stylised 3D level: a ruined granite temple courtyard inspired by Hampi, late afternoon. Exact layout: a square courtyard paved in big cracked stone slabs; at the far end a tall gopuram gateway with five tiers, its top tier broken off; on the left side a colonnade of six carved pillars, the third from the front fallen and lying across the paving; on the right a stepped stone water tank, empty and dry, with a small shrine at its corner; in the centre a stone chariot on four stone wheels. One grey placeholder cube sits by the chariot's right wheel. Low sun from the right throws long pillar shadows across the courtyard to the left. Camera at the courtyard entrance, standing height, 24 mm.

A lifestyle photo for a fictional smartwatch, the Sathi, in a Chennai park in early-morning golden light. A fictional woman of about sixty-eight with dark brown skin, grey hair in a braid, and a red bindi sits on a stone bench in a lilac cotton sari with a thin gold border and white sports shoes, glancing at the watch on her left wrist, smiling. The watch has a square black face showing "06:45" in white digits and a sage-green silicone strap. Behind her, a walking path, rain trees, and one man jogging far in the background on the right. Sun low from frame right. 85 mm, eye level.

A character key render for an original action game, full body, front three-quarter view facing frame left, standing on a dark wet rooftop with blurred magenta and cyan signs behind. The heroine, Ira, is a stylised 3D character with realistic proportions and a slightly painted finish. Dark brown skin, a high black ponytail bound with three gold rings, a thin gold nose ring on the left nostril. She wears a fitted charcoal armoured bodysuit with copper plates on the shoulders and shins, a short red sash-cape hanging from her right shoulder only, a glowing teal rune on the back of her left glove, and carries a curved single-edged sword with a brass guard shaped like a veena's head in her right hand, blade pointing down. Rim light from a magenta sign behind on the left, teal fill from the right.

A finished Diwali key visual for a fictional ghee brand, Saanjh Ghee, landscape. A glass jar of golden ghee with a gold lid stands dead centre. Its label is deep red with a gold border; on it the brand name "साँझ" in large gold Devanagari, "SAANJH GHEE" in small gold capitals below, and a round gold badge "500 ml" at the lower right of the label. In front of the jar, seven lit clay diyas stand in a shallow arc; marigold petals are scattered on a dark maroon surface; the background is a deep maroon with soft bokeh lights. Across the top, the headline "इस दिवाली, घर की ख़ुशबू" in cream Devanagari; under it, smaller, "Pure cow ghee since 1962" in cream. Bottom right, a gold starburst reading "₹349" and under it "Offer till 31 October" in small cream type. Warm light from the diyas on the jar.

A still from a coming-of-age feature set in rural Karnataka. Two Indian children, about ten years old, sit side by side on one thick exposed root at the base of a very old banyan tree. The boy sits on frame left, the girl on frame right, shoulders almost touching, both looking slightly off camera to frame left. The boy wears a white half-sleeve school shirt and navy shorts; short side-parted hair. The girl wears a white school shirt and a navy pinafore; her hair is in two plaits tied with red ribbons. A brown canvas school bag leans against the root just to the right of the girl. Hanging aerial roots frame the left third. Behind them on the right, a weathered wooden rail fence runs from mid-frame to the right edge, with a dry grass field beyond. Time is about twenty minutes before sunset: the sun is low behind the tree at upper frame right, so both children are backlit with warm rim light on hair and shoulders and their faces sit in soft open shade. Camera at the children's seated eye height, about six metres away, natural 35 mm perspective, the children in the lower middle of the frame and about a third of frame height. Fine film grain, soft warm haze, deep shadows under the canopy.

A product photo of a fictional hand-knitted elephant toy, Haathi, sitting on white, front three-quarter view. About 25 cm tall, knitted in soft grey wool, with stitched black button eyes, a curled trunk raised to its right, a small mustard knitted patch sewn on its left ear, and a red ribbon collar with a tiny brass bell. Visible knit texture. Soft even light. 85 mm.

A sportswear campaign frame at a city athletics stadium at harsh midday. A fictional Indian woman sprinter of about twenty-four is caught mid-stride in lane four of a red track, running left to right, side-on to the camera. She has short-cropped black hair, a determined look, and wears a sleeveless teal running vest and black shorts with no logos, a race bib reading "214" pinned to her vest, and white running shoes. Lane lines and the lane number "4" are painted on the track in white. Empty grey concrete stands behind. Hard overhead sun, short shadow directly beneath her. Camera at hip height, 85 mm, panning so she is sharp and the stands are slightly streaked.

A catalogue packshot of a fictional leather handbag, the Kosu Tote, on seamless off-white, in straight front view. A structured tote about 32 cm wide and 26 cm tall, in tan pebbled leather (close to #B5763A), with two rolled top handles in darker brown, a front flap closed by a brass turn-lock, contrast cream stitching along every edge, and a small blind-embossed "KOSU" on the front below the lock. One handle has a slight twist where it meets the bag; a few specks of dust on the flap. Soft light from upper left, a soft contact shadow under the base. 85 mm.

A small police-station interrogation room at night, lit only by one bare bulb under a conical green metal shade hanging low over a steel table. At the table on frame left sits the detective, a woman of about forty with short hair, in a maroon cotton kurta, a brown case file open in front of her. Opposite her on frame right sits the suspect, a man in his twenties in a torn grey T-shirt, a bruise on his left cheekbone, both hands flat on the table. Standing at the back by the closed door, slightly right of centre, a constable in khaki uniform with his arms folded. Green-painted walls with peeling patches, a wall calendar with blank pages, a steel water jug on the table. Hard top light, deep falloff, faces half in shadow. Camera at seated eye level from the side of the table, 35 mm.

A real-estate listing photo of the living room of a lived-in two-bedroom flat in a Mumbai tower, late morning, shot from the entrance corner at chest height with a 16 mm wide perspective, verticals kept straight. Exact layout: along the left wall, a grey three-seat fabric sofa facing right, with a framed abstract print above it and a pile of newspapers on its left cushion; at the back left, a doorway to the kitchen and beside it a tall snake plant in a white pot; the back wall is a sliding glass door to a narrow balcony, through which other towers and a laundry rack on the balcony are visible; on the right wall, a wall-mounted television, switched off, over a low white console with loose wires hanging below it; in the centre, a round wooden coffee table on a beige rug. White vitrified floor tiles, a ceiling fan and four recessed lights, all off. Daylight comes only from the balcony door.

A flat rooftop of an old Mumbai apartment block at night. A woman of about thirty in a loose white shirt and dark trousers leans with both forearms on the low parapet on frame right, looking out at the city, her face in three-quarter profile. Around her: three blue plastic water tanks on the left, a grey satellite dish on a stand at the back, a tangle of cables along the parapet. The city skyline glows orange-pink with scattered lit windows; a distant sodium streetlight below gives a faint orange edge on her right side. No other light. Camera at standing eye level, 35 mm, a few metres behind and to her left.

A 3D vehicle concept render of an original hover-bike in exact right side profile, facing frame right, floating half a metre above a dark reflective floor at night. A long low body in matte graphite with an orange stripe running from nose to tail, two round turbine pods under the front and rear glowing cyan underneath, a single curved windscreen, a seat with a quilted orange cover, and a white "07" decal on the rear fairing. A dent and scraped paint on the front fairing. Cool studio rim lights, the cyan glow reflected in the floor.

A concept artist's pencil and grey-marker sketch on white paper of an original game villain, Kaal, full body front view. A tall gaunt figure with a long black coat whose hem breaks into smoke-like ribbons, a cracked bronze half-mask covering the left side of his face, long white hair, a third eye drawn as a vertical glowing slit on his forehead, and a staff topped with a small hourglass held in his left hand. Thin construction lines are still visible around the figure. A small arrow note sketched beside the mask without words.

A finished cover for a fictional fashion magazine, ORBIT. A model of about thirty in a sculpted white blazer stands against a coral background, three-quarter length, slightly left of centre. The masthead "ORBIT" in tall black serif capitals across the top, partly behind her head. Cover lines on the right in a black condensed sans: "THE MONSOON EDIT", "48 looks for the rains", and in a small red box "Designers to watch: 10 new names". Bottom left: "OCTOBER 2026 · ₹150". Studio light from the left.

An empty hillside plot in North Goa at golden hour, shot from the access track at the bottom of the plot at standing height, 24 mm. The plot slopes gently up from the camera towards a ridge with a line of coconut palms. Exact layout: a red laterite stone survey marker in the lower left; two cashew trees in the middle of the plot, the left one larger; a dry stream bed running diagonally from the lower right up to the middle; a single electricity pole at the top right by the ridge; tall dry grass everywhere. Low sun from the right, long shadows to the left. The Arabian Sea is a thin blue line visible to the left of the ridge.

A realistic photograph-quality image: A screenshot of a simple retail web page with a header bar, a navigation row, a three-column product grid with names and prices, and a footer, rendered in a plain sans-serif on a light background. No watermark, no caption.

A realistic photograph-quality image: A hotel bedroom photographed from the doorway at eye level, showing a double bed against the far wall, two bedside tables, a desk with a chair under the window, a wardrobe on the near left wall and a luggage bench at the foot of the bed. No watermark, no caption.

An empty modern Indian kitchen dressed for a cooking commercial, late morning. Shot straight on from the open side at standing eye level, 28 mm. Layout, left to right: a tall white fridge; a window over a steel sink with a potted tulsi plant on the sill and soft daylight coming in; a long white quartz counter with a two-burner stove holding a steel kadhai and a pressure cooker; a wooden chopping board with chopped tomatoes and green chillies; open wall shelves of steel dabbas above the counter; a brass spice box (masala dabba) with its lid off on the right end of the counter. Pale sage-green cabinets below; white subway tiles behind. No people.

A catalogue flat-lay of a denim jacket on white, shot from directly above. Mid-blue stone-washed denim, a classic trucker cut with two chest pockets with pointed button flaps, copper buttons, and a hand-embroidered yellow marigold on the left chest pocket flap. The sleeves are folded in at the sides. The right cuff has a small frayed patch. Even light, true colour.

A festive advertising frame on the balcony of a Delhi apartment on Diwali evening, just after dusk. Exactly four people. A grandfather in a cream kurta and brown shawl sits on a cane chair on frame left; the mother, in a red silk sari, kneels in the centre lighting a row of seven clay diyas along the balcony ledge with a long matchstick; the father in a mustard kurta stands on frame right holding a steel plate of sweets; a girl of about seven in a green lehenga sits on the floor in front of the mother, finishing a round rangoli of pink, yellow and white powder. A string of warm fairy lights hangs along the top of the balcony railing; the city behind has scattered lights and one burst of fireworks in the upper right. The diyas are the main light, warm and low on all faces. Camera at standing eye level from inside the doorway, 35 mm.

A desert highway in Rajasthan at harsh midday. A man in his thirties sits astride a stopped classic black single-cylinder motorcycle on the road shoulder, seen from the front-right three-quarter view. The motorcycle has a round chrome headlamp, a black fuel tank with a visible dent on its right side, olive canvas saddlebags on both sides, and a red thread tied around the left handlebar grip. The rider wears aviator sunglasses, a brown leather jacket open over a white kurta, and dark trousers; he has a short beard. The straight road runs to a vanishing point at frame left; heat haze shimmers on the asphalt; scrub and low dunes on both sides; hard sun almost overhead, short dark shadows directly under bike and rider. Camera at standing eye level, 50 mm.

A frame from a Hindi television news broadcast. A fictional news anchor, a man of about forty with short grey-flecked hair, rectangular black glasses and a navy suit with a maroon tie, sits behind a curved white desk, medium shot, centred, looking into the lens. Behind him, a large screen shows a blurred city skyline. One soft key light from front left; a faint shadow of his head falls on the screen behind to his left. At the bottom, a red lower-third band reading "मुंबई में भारी बारिश" in white Devanagari, and below it a blue ticker reading "ट्रेनें 20 मिनट देरी से चल रही हैं". A small white clock "09:15" at the top right.

A vertical selfie-style frame of a fictional beauty creator of about twenty-three filming in her bedroom in Pune at night. Dark brown skin, a natural bare face, black hair pulled back in a claw clip, small gold hoops. She wears a sage-green ribbed tank top. Behind her, a white shelf crowded with bottles and a fairy-light string; in the mirror behind her on the right, the round ring light is reflected. The ring light in front is her key light, with catchlights as rings in both eyes. Phone-camera look, 26 mm equivalent, framed from mid-chest up.

A drone photo at about forty metres of a nearly finished 22-storey residential tower in Hyderabad at harsh noon, seen from the south-east. The tower is a slim rectangle with balconies on its south face (frame left) stacked in a zig-zag pattern, a plain east face (frame right) with a single vertical strip of small windows, and a lift-machine room on the roof painted blue. A yellow tower crane stands beside the north-east corner. At the base, a site office in white portable cabins and a green mesh fence around the plot; a main road with traffic along the bottom of the frame. Short hard shadows.

A product photo of a facade cladding sample on white: a 1.2 by 1.2 metre panel of horizontal terracotta louvres, each louvre a hollow rectangular tube 5 cm deep, in a warm burnt-orange with slight colour variation between louvres, spaced with even 3 cm gaps, mounted on a visible black aluminium sub-frame at the back. Three-quarter view from the left so the depth and the gaps show. Even light, soft shadow through the gaps. 85 mm.

A photo of a printed Hindi newspaper front page lying on a café table beside a cup of chai, seen from above at an angle, the paper slightly curled at the right edge so the headline bends. The masthead "नगर समाचार" in heavy black at the top. The main headline in large bold Devanagari across the top half: "शहर में नई मेट्रो लाइन शुरू". Under it a photo of a metro train and three columns of small body text. Soft daylight from a window on the left, a gentle shadow of the cup across the lower left of the page.

A product photo of a fictional running shoe, the DAUD One, on seamless white, right shoe only, in exact side profile with the toe pointing to frame right. Knit upper in coral (close to #FF6F59) fading to off-white at the heel; a thick white foam midsole with a single navy (close to #1D2A5B) stripe running its full length; a black rubber outsole; flat white laces; a small navy heel tab printed with "DAUD" in white capitals. Even soft studio light, a soft contact shadow under the sole. 85 mm, shoe filling three-quarters of the frame width.

A finished portrait event poster for a fictional night, on black. In the upper half, a DJ in profile under a single red light, hands raised on the decks. Text, exactly: across the middle in a huge condensed yellow sans "NIGHT SHIFT"; under it in white "with DJ KIRA"; then "SAT 14 DEC · 10 PM TILL LATE"; then a smaller line "Tickets ₹999 at the door"; at the bottom in small white capitals "THE BASEMENT, JUBILEE HILLS, HYDERABAD". A thin yellow frame runs round the poster's edge.

A furniture packshot of a fictional three-seat sofa on seamless white, front three-quarter view from the left. The sofa is 2.2 metres wide and 85 cm high, in rust-orange cotton-linen with three seat cushions, two bolster cushions in mustard at the arms, a low back and thin solid teak legs splayed outwards. Soft even light, soft contact shadow. 50 mm.

A marketplace listing infographic for a fictional steel water bottle, square, on a pale mint background. The bottle stands in the centre, matte navy with a bamboo cap. Four callouts with thin leader lines and simple line icons, two on each side: top left "Cold for 24 hours", bottom left "Hot for 12 hours", top right "100% leak-proof", bottom right "BPA-free steel". A headline across the top: "One bottle. All day." A small "1 litre" badge at the bottom centre. Clean rounded sans, dark navy text.

A widescreen film still at dawn. A man in his late fifties stands on a grassy ridge, seen in a medium-wide shot from his front-left, looking down into a valley below frame right. He has a short grey beard, a weathered face, and wears a long dark-charcoal wool coat, a rust-coloured knitted scarf and heavy brown boots. In his right hand he carries an old olive-green field radio with a long whip antenna; a canvas satchel hangs on his left hip. The valley below is filled with low fog, with three receding hill ridgelines fading into blue-grey. Pale gold sunlight from low frame left, cool shadows on the right of his face. Camera at chest height, 50 mm perspective, the man on the left third and three-quarters of frame height, horizon on the upper third. Muted desaturated palette, fine grain.

A finished app-store feature banner for the fictional game Shadow Raaga. On the right half, the heroine Ira (dark skin, high black ponytail with gold rings, charcoal armour, red cape on the right shoulder) leaps forward with her curved sword, against a stormy magenta and teal sky. On the left half, top to bottom: the game logo "SHADOW RAAGA" in tall angular silver letters with a thin teal glow; under it "Season 3: Monsoon Rift" in white; then a yellow rounded button reading "Pre-register now"; and at the bottom "Available 21 November" in small white type.

A theatrical one-sheet poster for a fictional English-language noir film. A silhouetted man in a hat stands under a single streetlight in heavy rain, small in the lower middle of the frame; deep black and teal palette. Exact text, nothing else: at the top, small spaced capitals "A FILM BY MEERA DAS"; across the upper third, the title "THE LAST MONSOON" in a tall condensed serif, cream colour; under it the tagline "Some debts are paid in rain." in italic; at the bottom a billing block in small condensed capitals reading "VIKRAM SETHI ANJALI ROY KABIR MALIK  MUSIC BY ARUN NAIR  CINEMATOGRAPHY BY LEELA IYER"; and under that "IN CINEMAS 14 NOVEMBER".

The front elevation of a contemporary two-storey villa in a Bengaluru gated community, shot straight on from the street at 1.6 metres with a 24 mm perspective and straight verticals, mid-morning sun from the left. Exact layout: a flat-roofed white box on the ground floor with a wide glass door on the right and a teak-clad wall on the left; a cantilevered upper floor in exposed grey concrete that overhangs the ground floor by about two metres on the right, holding a long horizontal window; a covered porch under the overhang with an empty wooden swing hanging on two chains; a black metal gate and a low granite boundary wall in the foreground; a frangipani tree on the left of the lawn. Clear blue sky.

A packshot of the fictional Saanjh Ghee jar on seamless cream, straight on at label height: a round glass jar of golden, slightly grainy ghee with a gold metal lid. Deep red label with a thin gold border; "साँझ" in large gold Devanagari; "SAANJH GHEE" in small gold capitals below; a round gold badge reading "500 ml" at the lower right of the label. Soft light from upper left, a vertical highlight on the glass on the left. 100 mm, jar filling two-thirds of the frame height.

A music-festival stage in Bengaluru at night, photographed from the front-of-house desk in the middle of the crowd, 35 mm, at standing height over the crowd's heads. A four-piece band: the singer, a woman in a silver jacket, at a centre microphone; a guitarist on stage left (frame left); a bassist on stage right; a drummer on a raised riser at the back centre. Behind them, a wide LED screen showing a slow orange and purple gradient. Two lighting trusses above the stage with moving heads throwing magenta beams from stage left and cyan beams from stage right through haze. In the foreground, the crowd's silhouettes, with three raised hands holding phones filming, their screens glowing.

A scanned page of rough storyboard thumbnails drawn quickly in blue pencil on off-white paper, six boxes in two rows of three, each numbered 1 to 6 in the top left corner. Simple stick-figure level drawing with hand-drawn arrows. Box 1: a wide market street, a running figure entering from the left edge. Box 2: a second figure vaulting over a fruit cart. Box 3: close view of running feet splashing on wet stones. Box 4: a top-down view of an alley junction with an arrow turning right. Box 5: the first figure hiding behind hanging cloth.
